description: A remote service terminates after roughly eighty bytes of input. The supplied executable is dynamically linked and ships with a companion shared library.
Sending longer and longer lines to the daemon eventually overwrites a function pointer stored next to a local array. No source is provided.
The process prints memory addresses when you insert percent signs into the greeting field. ASLR is enabled on the host.
You can free a note object twice from the menu. Afterward, allocating again lets you corrupt a pointer that used to belong to the note.
An executable rejects most passwords. Comparing two failing runs shows an early exit when the fifth character differs.
The program contains a large switch that dispatches on numeric opcodes read from a file. No symbols remain in the binary.
Strings that look like API names only appear after a small decoder loop runs over a byte table at startup.
Changing a browser cookie from role=user to role=admin grants access even though you never typed a password.
A search box reflects its contents into an HTML attribute without encoding. Angle brackets in the query change the page structure.
Uploading a file whose name contains ../ writes outside the uploads directory on the server.
The login form concatenates the password into a database query string. Supplying a quotation mark changes how many rows come back.
Two messages encrypted under the same stream key cancel when XOR'd together, revealing English-looking residue.
The server rejects some ciphertexts with 'padding error' and others with 'auth failed'. The difference is observable over the network.
A modulus factors in under a second on a laptop. The public exponent is three and the plaintext is short.
A packet capture of a short HTTP session is provided. The interesting payload is not in the first request.
An image file's metadata block is unusually large. Pixel data looks ordinary at a glance.
A memory snapshot from a laptop may still hold credentials that were never written to disk.
Only a username is given. The same handle appears on two public sites with overlapping profile photos.
A photo includes a visible street sign. No other context is provided.
The attachment decodes once to hexadecimal text and that text decodes again to a readable sentence.
Nested archives each ask for a short password derived from the previous layer's comment field.
A smart contract updates balances after an external call returns. Re-entering the withdraw function drains funds.
An Android package stores an API key in a resource file readable after unpacking the archive.
The daemon accepts a username then a password. Overlong usernames change which function runs after the prompt returns.
A local program reads a file path and copies its contents into a fixed-size region without checking length first.
You control the length field of a heap allocation. Setting it larger than the actual chunk lets neighboring metadata be rewritten.
The binary asks for a serial number. Wrong answers take different numbers of instructions before printing 'no'.
A packed-looking section unpacks itself into newly allocated memory before the real logic starts.
The admin panel is reachable if you send the same cookie the UI sets after login, even from a different browser profile.
Server-side rendering inserts the profile bio into a template language that evaluates expressions.
An API trusts the algorithm field inside a signed token header and will treat an empty signature as valid under one setting.
Identical plaintext blocks produce identical ciphertext blocks under this mode of operation.
Two signatures share the same ephemeral value; algebra recovers the private key from the pair.
A repeating single-byte key was used on a short English sentence; frequency of the most common byte is revealing.
A disk image contains deleted files whose headers still match known document types.
Network traffic includes DNS queries for unusual hostnames that encode parts of a message.
A company email domain is known. Public certificate logs list additional hostnames under that domain.
The puzzle is only a sequence of Morse-like dots and dashes in a text file.
Anyone can call a privileged function because ownership is checked only in the web UI, not in the contract.
Decompiling the mobile app shows hardcoded endpoints and a bearer token in a constants class.
Cross-origin requests succeed with credentials because the server reflects any Origin and allows credentials.
After leaking a library address from a write primitive, you need a chain of return addresses to call system.
Anti-analysis code exits early when a debugger is detected via timing of a short loop.
Broadcast encryption of the same message under related moduli allows recovery without the private keys.
A chat export contains timestamps and GPS-like coordinates embedded in message metadata.
A nickname from an old forum post matches a developer account that still lists a personal blog.
Each layer of the archive is compressed with a different tool; the final payload is plain text.
A GraphQL endpoint answers introspection queries and returns fields the official client never requests.
The service installs a syscall filter before reading input; only a few system calls remain allowed.
Go runtime metadata is still present and can be used to recover function names the strip step left behind.
The binary greets you and then reads a line. Values past the end of the greeting buffer alter the return address observed in a debugger.
Only open, read, and write remain after the filter installs. Building a shell requires staying inside that set.
Floating-point constants in the data section match coefficients of a known checksum polynomial.
A Rust-built binary still embeds panic strings that name internal modules.
Password reset tokens are predictable integers. Requesting consecutive values resets other accounts.
The application deserializes a cookie with a library known to invoke gadget chains when type fields are attacker-controlled.
Nonce reuse in an authenticated encryption scheme lets an observer recover the authentication key material.
A classical cipher over English leaves digram frequencies almost unchanged from plaintext.
A browser profile directory still holds cookies and form history after the user thought they logged out.
Carve tools recover a JPEG from unallocated space; EXIF still contains a phone model string.
A resume PDF lists an old personal domain. The domain's historical WHOIS is still in public archives.
The only attachment is a QR code image that decodes to another short encoded string.
Integer underflows in a token accounting function mint extra balance when amounts wrap.
Certificate pinning is implemented in Java but a debug build disables the pin check when a flag file exists.
File uploads accept SVG. Script inside the SVG executes when an admin opens the avatar page.
Partial overwrite of a pointer is possible because only two bytes differ between the heap and a libc address.
Control flow flattens into a dispatcher state machine; recovering the original order needs the state variable.
Related-key messages under a short repeating pad are solvable by crib-dragging known headers.
A hibernation file from Windows may still contain plaintext documents from the last session.
Satellite imagery timestamps and shadow direction roughly confirm when an outdoor photo was taken.
Websocket messages are not authenticated. Replaying a prior admin message performs privileged actions.
A programming challenge judges only stdout; the intended solution is a short golfed script, not exploitation.
The canary is leaked through an off-by-one that does not kill the process immediately.
Dotnet assemblies retain method names unless obfuscated; a decompiler shows the license check clearly.
Small private exponents make Wiener's attack practical against the public key file provided.
USB attachment logs on the host show a mass-storage device serial that matches a suspect's keychain drive.
Cache poisoning makes a shared CDN serve a page with an injected header to other users.
Randomness for a card game on-chain uses a predictable block hash that miners can influence.
Frida can bypass the root detection branch that only returns a boolean checked in one activity.
An image board post includes a reflection of a skyline usable to identify the city.
The service echoes input and then crashes only when the fifth argument to a format-like specifier is used.
Global offset table entries can be rewritten after a write primitive is obtained from a heap bug.
Virtual machine bytecode is interpreted in a loop; recovering the program means understanding the opcodes.
License check compares a transformed serial to a constant embedded near the end of the text segment.
HTTP request smuggling works because the front proxy and the back app disagree on chunked encoding.
A hidden field stores the price of a cart item; changing it on the client changes the charged amount.
Common modulus attacks apply when the same message is encrypted to two public exponents sharing n.
An ECB mode image encrypts each block independently, leaving silhouettes visible in ciphertext.
Prefetch files on Windows indicate which binaries were run and when on the suspect machine.
A pcapng of TLS traffic still leaks hostnames via the server name indication extension.
A vehicle plate in a photo can be cross-checked against a regional format to narrow the country.
The challenge is a logic puzzle stated in prose; no binary or network service is involved.
A flash-loan pattern drains a pool because the invariant is checked before the loan is repaid.
Exported activities in the manifest can be launched by third-party apps without authentication.
Host header injection makes password-reset links point at an attacker-controlled domain.
Stack alignment must be corrected before a movaps instruction in the libc path succeeds.
Opaque predicates always take the same branch; simplifying them reveals the real control flow.
Franklin-Reiter related-message attack applies to two RSA ciphertexts under a known linear relation.
Slack export ZIP files include channel histories with deleted messages still present in the JSON.
A Git commit email in a public repo matches a personal account that still hosts the same avatar.
A networked binary greets you by name. Names longer than the prompt area change which instruction runs after the function returns.
Submitting a math expression in the profile field evaluates on the server and the result appears in the rendered page.
The program asks for a license key. Wrong keys take a different number of milliseconds before rejection.
Two messages under the same keystream cancel when combined, revealing structure of the original language.
A browser profile directory may still hold session tokens after the user closed the window.
